derivations.claim:
Identify $\mathbb C^d$ with $\mathbb R^{2d}$ by real and imaginary
coordinates. Its unit sphere is a closed bounded subset and is nonempty
because $d\ge1$; it is compact by [F1].

The Rayleigh function $f(x)=x^*Ax$ is real on the unit sphere, since
$A=A^*$, and is continuous because each coordinate of $f$ is a finite
polynomial in the real and imaginary coordinates of $x$. By [F2] it has a
maximizer $u$ with $u^*u=1$.

Fix $w$ with $u^*w=0$ and let
$g(t)=(u+tw)^*A(u+tw)/(u+tw)^*(u+tw)$ for real $t$. The denominator is
$1+t^2w^*w>0$, so $g$ is differentiable near $0$; maximality of $u$ gives
$g'(0)=0$. Expanding numerator and denominator gives
$g'(0)=2\operatorname{Re}(w^*Au)$, hence the real part of $w^*Au$ is zero.

Apply step 3.1 with $iw$ in place of $w$. Since $(iw)^*Au=-i\,w^*Au$,
its real part is the imaginary part of $w^*Au$; therefore $w^*Au=0$ for
every $w\perp u$. Decompose $Au=(u^*Au)u+w_0$ with $w_0\perp u$; taking
$w=w_0$ yields $w_0^*Au=\|w_0\|^2=0$. Thus $Au=\lambda u$, where
$\lambda=u^*Au\in\mathbb R$.

If $x\perp u$, then $u^*Ax=(Au)^*x=\lambda u^*x=0$, so $u^\perp$ is
invariant under $A$ and the restriction of $A$ to it is Hermitian. For $d=1$
the standard unit vector is already an eigenbasis. For $d>1$, induction on
the dimension supplies an orthonormal eigenbasis on $u^\perp$; adjoining
$u$ gives one for $\mathbb C^d$.

For any unit eigenvector $v$ with eigenvalue $\mu$, positivity gives
$\mu=v^*Av\ge0$. By [F3], each such $\mu$ has a unique nonnegative square
root. In the eigenbasis from step 5.1, define $A^{1/2}$ to be diagonal with
entries $\sqrt{\mu}$. This matrix is nonnegative and squares to $A$; it is
independent of choices inside repeated eigenspaces because the same scalar
is assigned to every vector in that eigenspace.

derivations.claim:
For $N\ge2$, let $\pi_N$ be the diagonal density uniform on binary
strings with even parity, and let $\gamma_N=I/2^N$. There are $2^{N-1}$
even strings: the first $N-1$ bits can be arbitrary and the last bit is
uniquely determined. Fix $k<N$ coordinates and their values. Among the
$N-k\ge1$ unassigned coordinates, exactly half of the $2^{N-k}$ completions
have the required parity, namely $2^{N-k-1}$. Summing by [F1], the marginal
probability of each fixed $k$-bit string is
$2^{N-k-1}/2^{N-1}=2^{-k}$. Thus
$(\pi_N)_k=I/2^k=(\gamma_N)_k$ for every proper block.

On an even string the diagonal difference $\pi_N-\gamma_N$ is
$2^{-(N-1)}-2^{-N}=2^{-N}$; on an odd string it is $-2^{-N}$. There are
$2^N$ strings in total, so the absolute eigenvalues sum to
$2^N2^{-N}=1$. Therefore $\|\pi_N-\gamma_N\|_1=1$ for every $N$.

Let $P_{\rm even}$ be the diagonal projection onto even strings. Then
$(P_{\rm even},I-P_{\rm even})$ is a two-outcome POVM by [F2]. Its first
outcome has probability $1$ in $\pi_N$ and $1/2$ in $\gamma_N$, a gap of
$1/2$. Hence equality of all proper local marginals does not entail global
trace-norm convergence or equality of global measurement predictions.
